paragraphs.text: A dsh-TUI plugin that pins the model, reasoning effort, agent preset and permission mode every new c
onversation starts on, plus a /favors command to inspect or re-apply them on demand.
# dsh-tui-favors
Pin the four values a dsh-TUI launch starts on — **model route, reasoning effort, agent preset and p
ermission mode** — so every launch returns to your favorites instead of whatever the last session ha
ppened to end on. Turn on `pin: true` to extend that to every `/new` within the same run.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart dsh-TUI afterwards: the row writes the preference files during startup.
## Use
Favorites come from two layers with the same shape: your profile's row config, and an optional `~/.d
sh-tui/favors.json` that wins key by key.
### Layer 1 — the profile row
Add your favorites to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (any knob you leave out is not touched):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Layer 2 — `~/.dsh-tui/favors.json`
Flat JSON, the same keys as the `config:` block above, sitting next to `model.json` and friends:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It applies without a restart when `pin: true` (each check re-reads it, 2 s by default); with the def
ault `pin: false` a new or edited file is picked up on the next launch or by `/favors apply`. Knobs
you leave out keep the row's value, and a value that fails validation is reported instead of applied
— the row's value stays, so a typo never silently un-pins a knob. A whole copy-pasted patch row (wi
th `id`/`name`/`config`) is refused with a hint to keep only the keys inside `config`. `enabled: fal
se` on the profile row is a kill switch: the file is then not even read.
Then, inside the TUI:
- `/favors` — show each knob: the pinned value, its source (`[favors.json]` or `[profile row]`), wha
t the preference file currently holds, and whether something outranks it (`DSH_TUI_PRESET`, `DSH_PER
MISSION_MODE`, the `/settings` default effort). The `source:` line reports whether the file is missi

ng, in effect, or ignored.
- `/favors apply` — re-read the file and rewrite the four files immediate
ly instead of waiting for the next launch or `pin` check.
With `pin: false` (the default) the files are written once per launch: a mid-session `/model`, `/eff
ort`, `/preset` or `/permission` pick stays in effect, and the next `/new` re-reads it — the favorit
es are back on the next launch. Set `pin: true` to revert those picks, which is what makes every `/n
ew` start on the favorites; `pollMs` (2 s by default) then decides how quickly. It costs one `stat`
per check and nothing else.
Two limits worth knowing: reasoning effort is pinned per launch (dsh-TUI caches the preferred tier i
n-process, so an in-session `/effort` lasts until the next start), and `permission.json` only seeds
sessions that never picked a permission mode themselves.
